name: Omnitech Engineering Ltd
tagline: Recently-listed small-cap precision-engineered components (machining/forging/casting) exporter with strong revenue growth (~92% YoY) but stretched valuation (~84x P/E, ~9.5x book) and rising leverage - growth is real but already priced in.
business_overview: Omnitech Engineering manufactures high-precision engineered components and assemblies (machining, grinding, turning, sub-assembly across carbon/alloy/stainless steel, nickel alloys, titanium, aluminium) for 250+ customers across ~24 countries, serving energy, motion-control/automation and industrial-equipment end markets. NOTE: a separate, unrelated listed entity, Omnitech Infosolutions Ltd (an IT services micro-cap, market cap ~Rs 1.6 Cr, negative ROE/ROCE), also trades under a similar name - this write-up is for Omnitech Engineering Ltd (NSE: OMNI), the entity judged the far more plausible match for the bullish X mention given Infosolutions' distressed/dormant state; this identification is not 100% certain and should be re-confirmed if used for a serious position. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@ParthaAwe, bullish/medium conviction, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: FY25 revenue ~Rs 343 Cr vs ~Rs 178 Cr FY24 (+92%); FY26 consolidated revenue +49.1% YoY to ~Rs 511 Cr
fundamentals_narrative: Omnitech Engineering is a genuine growth story - revenue nearly doubled FY24-FY25 (~Rs 178 Cr to ~Rs 343 Cr) and grew a further ~49% YoY in FY26 (~Rs 511 Cr) - with a broad, global (24-country) precision-components customer base that plausibly benefits from China+1/supply-chain-diversification demand. But the growth is already very fully priced: ~84x trailing P/E and ~9.5x book value leave little margin of safety, and leverage (debt/equity ~63%) plus elevated debtor days (~172) are real balance-sheet cautions for a recently-listed small-cap. This looks like a strong operating story trading at a valuation that already assumes the growth continues without a stumble.
